headline: Biologically constrained models attribute cortical phenomena to specific components
label: Interpretable Neural Encoding Models
summary: Recent preprints and publications attribute V1 contextual modulation, representational drift, and invariant object learning to individual model components.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of explicitly constrained, biologically motivated encoding models to account for specific cortical response properties. TAVAE, a VAE with task-amortized adaptable priors, models V1 contextual modulation and is validated against mouse V1 recordings. A partial information decomposition of two public datasets links tuning stability to pairwise redundancy in representational drift, using information-theoretic measures of neural and behavioural coupling. A biologically plausible four-layer competitive network with a local trace learning rule addresses transform-invariant object and face learning from V1 along the ventral pathway. What is new is the attribution of particular phenomena to particular model components, such as adaptable priors or local learning rules. The items do not share a single method, so the thread is mechanistic interpretability of cortical representations rather than a shared benchmark.
